The average is the mean order count over accounts that have orders. Output is account id, region A3, order count, and count minus average. Sort is by difference descending, returning the top 10 plus all ties with the 10th value
Same as 1, but the average is computed after the join to district, so only accounts with a matching district are averaged. This differs only if some accounts have no district match

The average is taken over all accounts in the `account` table, including those with no orders. This contradicts the "accounts that have orders" wording, but it is a possible reading
The average is taken per region, as the mean order count of accounts in the same A3 region, and the difference is measured against that regional average
The average is taken per district rather than overall

queries:
WITH oc AS (
    SELECT a.account_id, d.A3 AS region, COUNT(*) AS order_count
    FROM "order" o
    JOIN account a ON o.account_id = a.account_id
    JOIN district d ON a.district_id = d.district_id
    GROUP BY a.account_id, d.A3
),
avgc AS (
    SELECT AVG(order_count) AS avg_count FROM oc
),
ranked AS (
    SELECT oc.account_id, oc.region AS A3, oc.order_count,
           oc.order_count - avgc.avg_count AS diff
    FROM oc, avgc
)
SELECT account_id, A3, order_count, diff
FROM ranked
WHERE diff >= (SELECT diff FROM ranked ORDER BY diff DESC LIMIT 1 OFFSET 9)
ORDER BY diff DESC;
SELECT CAST(COUNT(order_id) AS REAL) / COUNT(DISTINCT account_id) FROM `order`;
SELECT AVG(order_count) FROM (SELECT a.account_id, COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_count FROM account a LEFT JOIN `order` o ON a.account_id = o.account_id GROUP BY a.account_id);
WITH account_orders AS (
    SELECT a.account_id, d.A3 AS region, COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_count
    FROM account a
    JOIN district d ON a.district_id = d.district_id
    LEFT JOIN `order` o ON a.account_id = o.account_id
    GROUP BY a.account_id, d.A3
)
SELECT account_id,
       order_count - AVG(order_count) OVER (PARTITION BY region) AS difference
FROM account_orders;
